title: Maps
bridge: C++'s dictionary is `std::map<Key, Value>` (sorted by key) or `std::unordered_map` (faster, no order). `m["maize"] += 5;` creates the entry at 0 if it's missing. `m.count(k)` says if a key exists; loop with `for (auto& [key, value] : m)`.

exercises.title: Word counts
exercises.prompt: Write std::map<std::string, int> wordCounts(std::string text): how many times each word appears (words are split by spaces).

exercises.title: Most common word
exercises.prompt: Write std::string mostCommon(std::string text): the word that appears most (on a tie, the one first alphabetically). Empty text gives "".

tests.hint_if_fail: std::map is sorted, so walking it meets 'a' first; only replace the best on a strictly bigger count.

hints: Count first (like the last exercise), then walk the map keeping the best.
if (n > bestCount) { best = w; bestCount = n; }
